axes_culturels.description: The boundaries between private and public life, their evolution in contemporary English-speaking societies.
exemples_objets_etude: Right to be forgotten and personal data
Architecture and urban planning (gated communities, public spaces)

axes_culturels.description: The construction of territories and collective memories in the English-speaking world, between heritage and conflicts.
exemples_objets_etude: The Berlin Wall / the USA-Mexico wall
Sites of remembrance and memorial tourism

axes_culturels.description: The relationship between fiction and reality: how works of fiction reflect, question or transform reality in English-speaking culture.
exemples_objets_etude: Dystopias and speculative fiction (Orwell, Atwood, Ishiguro)

axes_culturels.description: Transformations in communication and their implications (media, political, interpersonal) in English-speaking societies.
exemples_objets_etude: Political rhetoric and speeches (I have a dream, Yes we can)

axes_culturels.description: Exercising citizenship in digital and virtual worlds, between opportunities and pitfalls.

axes_culturels.titre: The United Kingdom and its nations
axes_culturels.description: Study of the United Kingdom in its national diversity (England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland): identities, tensions, common future. Compulsory axis.
exemples_objets_etude: Brexit and its consequences on UK unity
The Northern Irish conflict and the peace process
The British monarchy: tradition and modernity

contraintes.note: 5 out of 6 axes must be covered during the year, including axis 6 (The United Kingdom and its nations) which is compulsory.

comprehension_orale.descripteur: Understand extended speech even when not clearly structured, understand TV programmes and films without too much effort.

comprehension_ecrite.descripteur: Understand long, complex factual or literary texts, appreciate differences in style, understand specialised articles.

expression_orale.descripteur: Give a clear, well-structured presentation with clear argumentation, depart spontaneously from a prepared text and follow up on audience reactions.

expression_ecrite.descripteur: Write clear, detailed texts, an argumentative essay, a review, a professional report with a stated position.

interaction.descripteur: Actively participate in formal or informal discussion, negotiate, argue convincingly, react to others' arguments.

mediation.descripteur: Summarise, synthesise and reliably convey information and arguments from multiple sources, adapt discourse to context.

grammaire: Subjunctive (I suggest that he go…, if I were…)
Stylistic inversion (Not only… but also, Hardly had… when)
Advanced epistemic and deontic modals (shall, ought to, need, dare)
Ellipsis and substitution (so do I, neither can they)
Complex reported speech (varied reporting verbs: urged, insisted, denied + -ing)
Mixed conditionals (If I had studied / I would be…)
Perfect aspect and its nuances (have been doing vs have done vs did)
